blocks.text: primum auctorem habuisse Constantinum, Romanorum imperatorem, qui الشواهين sahinos habuerit supra caput suum volare edoctos, et umbram ipsi facere, ne a solis aestu torreretur. Sed et librum Gallicum penes me habeo, cui titulus, Conference des fauconniers, id est, Accipitrariorum collatio. In eo sahini collatione decima sic describuntur: Les sahins sont des faucons de haute maille, qui ont la teste plate au dessus, et le pennage bordè de blanc, et encores egalè de roux. Dont il semble, que la nature leur ait mis sur la teste une guirlan- de, ou couronne, pour marque de leur excellence. Bref, ce sont les faucons, qu'anciennement on nommoit pelerins, ou faucons Tartares, bien que ce fut im- proprement parlè ^{(4)}. Et amplissimus Thuanus, postquam Peregrinum vocari dixit, quia natales habet incertos, eum ita describit Rei accipitrariae libri primi pagina decima quarta,

blocks.text: Digna sunt, quae huc apponantur, quae de شاهين habet RUSSELL in the Natural History of the city of Aleppo p. 68. „For bird-hawking, they use a large falcon, with long legs, somewhat like the goshawk, which they call espeer; and two smaller falcons, stiled the one Zan- ous, and the other shaheen. This latter must be taken out of the nest, for when old they cannot be trained, and is so fier- ce, that it will fly at ang thing. If there were not several gentlemen now in Eng- land, who can attest it, I should scarce ventnre to mention, that with the shaheen, which is about the size of a pigeon, they often take the largest eagles, of which in this country there are plenty. They for- merly were trained to seize the eagle un- der the wing: and so depriving him of the use of that part, they fell to the ground together: but their present method, as I am informed, is to seize him on the back between the two wings, which has the sa- me effect, but brings him down more slowly, and so gives the falconer time, to come in to his hawk's assistance; in which if he is not very expeditious, the hawk is in either case speedily destroyed.“
